items.title: One tooth, six clues: How a single tooth can help in identifying deceased persons
items.text: A single tooth can contain valuable clues to a person's identity, even when remains are severely decomposed or reduced to bones, according to a study by researchers at the Institute of Science Tokyo. By applying multiple forensic methods to different tissues within a single tooth, the researchers obtained six types of information about the deceased. This integrated approach could provide complementary evidence to help identify unknown human remains when conventional methods are difficult to apply.
items.summary_th: นักวิจัยจาก Institute of Science Tokyo พบว่าการใช้วิธีทางนิติวิทยาศาสตร์กับฟันเพียงซี่เดียวสามารถระบุข้อมูลของผู้เสียชีวิตได้ถึง 6 ด้าน แม้ศพจะเน่าเปื่อยอย่างรุนแรง

items.title: AI identifies tumor aging patterns to predict immunotherapy response across multiple cancer types
items.text: Even when given the same drug, some patients respond well while others show little or no response. This is particularly true of immunotherapy. A research team at POSTECH (Pohang University of Science and Technology) has developed an artificial intelligence (AI) technology that can predict, in advance, which patients are likely to benefit from treatment.

items.title: Death rates among 25–49-year-olds 42% higher in the North than the South of England, study finds
items.text: Death rates among adults ages 25–49 were 42% higher in the North than in the South of England in 2024, compared with 13% higher in 1981, according to research published today in The Lancet Public Health.
